text.en: For every rated wall, you should be able to answer
What exact approved assembly is this supposed to be?

identify all rated walls on plan;
Framing → first-side board → services/penetrations → insulation/internal components → opposite-side board → joints/firestop → final condition
This prevents trying to inspect an entire assembly after everything has disappeared.

A board that looks like drywall does not establish that it is the specified fire-rated component.
Photographs should be taken before concealment, not merely after painting.

Identify affected wall/extent → control further finishing → document assembly requirement → remove/open as necessary → install missing approved layer → reinspect configuration → restore joints/finishes → document → close.
Repeated deficiencies should trigger earlier inspection/intervention rather than simply producing more NCRs.

qualityObjective.en:
This should be one of the most rigorous modules in the entire application.
The central concept is:
Firestop is not “red caulking around a pipe.” It is an approved system consisting of a specific assembly, opening, penetrating item, annular space, backing/fill material, firestop material, required depth/configuration and installation conditions.

Track interface failures separately because they often reveal coordination problems rather than workmanship problems.

new penetration → identify rated wall → establish applicable approved firestop system → inspect installation → photograph → update penetration register → restore wall's quality status
This is precisely why a systematic inspector catches things that a purely reactive inspector can miss.
Sprinkler head location becomes obstructed after a large duct is installed.
Your role is not to invent a new sprinkler location.

Document condition → compare approved coordinated drawings → notify Responsable qualité → coordinate fire-protection/mechanical teams → obtain authorized resolution → implement → inspect physical correction → obtain required specialist verification → close.
If something that determines fire performance is about to disappear, that is your last inexpensive opportunity to prove it was constructed correctly.
WHAT SYSTEM APPLIES?→ approved/listed system reference
DO THE ACTUAL DIMENSIONS FIT THAT SYSTEM?→ opening + penetrating item + annular space
WHAT WAS INSTALLED?→ backing + product + depth/configuration
WHAT PROVES IT?→ inspection + photos + label
WAS IT MODIFIED LATER?→ reopen/reinspect if yes
That is the level of traceability I would want in our Hochelaga system.

3. Sweep the wall physically from one end to the other.
This should be one of the strongest STOP/CHECK gates in the whole application.
